title: The Next AI Revolution Is Here… THIS is the ONE Stock I'm Buying
creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
summary: Joseph Hogue follows up his 9 October Robo Strategy video with a long interview with Andrew Kang, CEO of Robo Strategy — the Nasdaq-listed closed-end fund trading under ticker BOT — framing BOT in the title as the one stock he is buying for the robotics wave. Kang argues physical AI is the missing intelligence piece that now makes robotics viable: the physical labour market is a ~$50 trillion proxy, Morgan Stanley's base case is ~$5 trillion with nearly a billion humanoids, and the bottom-up math is stark — 100,000 humanoids at $50,000 is ~$5 billion of revenue, a million is ~$50 billion, ten million ~$500 billion. The portfolio spans general-purpose humanoids (Figure AI — praised for founder Brett Adcock's record, a team drawn from Boston Dynamics, Tesla and DeepMind, and unprecedented development speed), intelligent robot arms/cobots, the actuator supply chain (30–50% of a robot's bill of materials, no mature supply chain yet) and application-specific names like Path Robotics, whose AI welding business just won a $600 million contract with shipbuilder HII. On the fund itself: the closed-end structure exists because the holdings are private and long-term; NAV is marked off last financing rounds, so it lags by 12–24 months; the fund trades at a premium to NAV, and Kang's 'multiple arbitrage' engine issues shares at that premium and redeploys the cash to lift NAV per share — NAV/share is up over 50% (~55%) in about four months since launch, mostly from that mechanism rather than markups. Fees: 2.5% management fee, expense ratio slightly higher on one-time listing costs expected to compress, and no performance fee versus the VC 2-and-20 model. Bear case as discussed: manufacturing capacity is the binding bottleneck, AI timelines could slip by years, and the premium can shrink or flip. Timeline: hundreds of thousands to millions of robots in manufacturing within two years, tens to hundreds of millions by the early 2030s, homes late-2020s/early-2030s. Call made: BOT — BUY reiterated; no market price stated. Caption garbles include 'Robbo Strategy', 'Atronic/Optronic' for Apptronik and 'GBDT' for GPT, so names were sanity-checked against the 9 October video.

calls.thesis: Reiterated BUY (first tracked 9 Oct): follow-up interview with Robo Strategy CEO Andrew Kang; title frames BOT as 'the ONE stock I'm buying' — the Nasdaq closed-end fund as the vehicle for pre-IPO robotics/physical-AI exposure (Figure AI, Apptronik, Dyna Robotics, Standard Bots, Path Robotics). Kang: NAV/share up >50% (~55%) in ~4 months since launch, driven mostly by crystallising the NAV premium via new issuance ('multiple arbitrage'), not markups; fund trades at a premium to NAV today.
calls.price_at_call: no market price stated; 2.5% management fee (expense ratio a bit higher on one-time listing costs, expected to compress); premium-to-NAV is the central risk
